sources.title: The Federated States of Micronesia Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.organization: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate and adaptation assessment published September 2025; includes 2024 population and water-service information.
sources.methodology: National government submission to UNFCCC; policy report.
sources.limitations: Commitments and needs are not independently evaluated.

sources.title: Climate Change in the Federated States of Micronesia: Food and Water Security, Climate Risk Management, and Adaptive Strategies—Report of Findings 2010
sources.organization: University of Hawaiʻi Sea Grant College Program, Center for Island Climate Adaptation and Policy, with the U.S. Geological Survey
sources.temporal_coverage: Three-week field assessment in April 2009, including retrospective accounts of 2002 and 2007–2008 hazards.
sources.methodology: Three-week field assessment in April 2009, combining interviews, community visits, and literature review.
sources.limitations: Short field period and older hazard conditions; not a representative survey or updated risk model.

sources.title: Federated States of Micronesia: 2026 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Federated States of Micronesia
sources.organization: International Monetary Fund, Asia and Pacific Department
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 Article IV consultation; climate-risk assessment, governance and fragility analysis, and adaptation discussion.
sources.methodology: IMF staff Article IV report and fragility annex; only relevant climate and governance passages used.
sources.limitations: Only substantive official publisher-indexed excerpts were accessible, not the full report body.

claims.paraphrase: NDC says coastal and atoll communities 1–2 m above sea level face sea-level rise, drought, erosion and stronger storms; shocks are eroding assets and farm/fishing livelihoods.
institutions: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia
claims.limitations: No local prevalence or climate-attribution estimate.

claims.paraphrase: Low-lying islands rely on rainwater and shallow wells; drought risk is named for Yap and western Chuuk. The NDC reports utility drinking water reaches about 8% of Weno households versus 96% of Pohnpei residents.
claims.limitations: NDC-reported utility coverage; not independently rechecked.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 17 and 20, §§4.5–4.6, Governance and Land Ownership
claims.paraphrase: State governments manage land, coast, health, education, water and roads. Yap includes traditional leaders in government; the NDC says tenure matters for adaptation/relocation and can hinder infrastructure.
claims.limitations: Governance context; conflict outcomes are unmeasured.

claims.paraphrase: NDC says financing covers 25% of adaptation needs; insufficient technical capacity hinders implementation.
affected_groups: communities and ecosystems targeted by adaptation policies
institutions: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia

claims.locator: PDF p. 25 (printed p. 22), Pohnpei State Findings
claims.paraphrase: The field report says Pohnpei’s outer atoll islets Pingelap, Mokil, Ant, Pakin, Ngatik, Nukuoro and Kapingamarangi suffered extreme hardship during 2007–08 marine inundation.
claims.limitations: The report is a 2009 field assessment recalling earlier events.

claims.locator: PDF p. 25 (printed p. 22), Chuuk State Findings
claims.paraphrase: In Chuuk, Tropical Storm Chataan’s 2002 heavy rain caused over 30 landslides and 47 deaths. The report describes poor roads and unpotable drinking water; high tides and runoff filled potholes on the coastal business-district road.
claims.limitations: Hazard and service conditions are historical, not a current status assessment.

claims.locator: PDF p. 26 (printed p. 23), Yap State Findings
claims.paraphrase: In Yap, 2007–08 surges damaged coastal infrastructure, food and housing; the report says main-island water remained nonpotable and harbor protections were only 30–60 cm above high tide.
claims.limitations: The report reflects 2009 conditions and does not establish present-day exposure.

claims.locator: Annex IV, Climate Change risk row; risk discussion ¶8
claims.paraphrase: The IMF risk matrix states that climate disasters damage infrastructure and livelihoods, worsen food insecurity, and delay development as scarce resources shift to response and reconstruction.
claims.limitations: IMF staff risk assessment; not community-level causal research.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The risk matrix says disasters set back development as thin institutional capacity is redirected to recovery and reconstruction.

claims.locator: §C, Climate-Change Resilience, ¶28; Annex I, Drivers of Fragility, ¶¶2–4
claims.paraphrase: IMF says adaptation progress is constrained by limited institutional capacity, fragmented interagency coordination, and weak climate-risk integration in fiscal and infrastructure planning; it also identifies political fragmentation and administrative capacity as fragility drivers.
institutions: Office of the National Public Auditor
claims.limitations: IMF staff synthesis; effects are not quantified by state or community.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The IMF states that institutional and coordination constraints have constrained climate-adaptation progress.

access_audit.notes: Published September 2025; the government NDC reports planned measures as commitments, not evaluated outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; original paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: The report describes three weeks of April 2009 field assessment and 2002/2007–2008 hazard events.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; original paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: Search-indexed official passages were inspected; opening the full eLibrary body did not provide full-text access. Claims are limited to those excerpts.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; original paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: The indexed passage describes atoll saltwater intrusion and high-island land-tenure limits; full PDF body was not opened and the excerpt is not used for claims.

access_audit.locator: PDF landing/search result for the 2023 PIRCA report.
access_audit.notes: The 80-page, approximately 12 MB PDF could not be rendered by the browser tool; no report claims are used.

search_audit.query: FSM state and outer-island climate vulnerability water food roads named atolls primary reports
search_audit.outcome: The full 2025 NDC provides state-specific water access and drought information; the 2010 field report names Pohnpei outer atolls and describes historic Chuuk and Yap impacts. A complete contemporary island-by-island vulnerability ranking was not located.

search_audit.query: FSM climate hazards fragility conflict food livelihoods land tenure political tensions report
search_audit.outcome: The IMF report explicitly links climate disasters to diverted institutional capacity and delayed development, and discusses political fragmentation under its fragility diagnosis. No inspected source establishes a climate-driven violent-conflict incidence or local violence pathway.

search_audit.query: FSM political fragmentation inter-state resource allocation adaptation planning capacity governance 2026 IMF
search_audit.outcome: The IMF fragility annex says decentralized decision-making, capacity constraints and political fragmentation impede reform and generate tensions around state resource allocation; its climate section says institutional and coordination limits constrain adaptation. No source explicitly links armed insecurity to climate-response delivery.

search_audit.query: FSM community resilience adaptation water security traditional knowledge disaster preparedness response capacity
search_audit.outcome: The NDC describes adaptation measures and state water practices but notes a 25% adaptation-financing coverage and technical-capacity constraint; the older assessment details locally relevant needs. The 2023 PIRCA full report was not accessible, and evaluated community outcomes remain thin.

gaps: No inspected source establishes a countrywide causal estimate of climate effects on conflict or violence; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
The 2010 field assessment supplies detailed named-state evidence but is historical; recent complete island-level hazard, displacement and service-access coverage was not found.
The full 2023 PIRCA report PDF was not accessible through the browser retrieval path; no claims rely on its search metadata.
The 2025 NDC reports adaptation-financing and technical-capacity constraints but does not independently evaluate implementation outcomes.
The 2026 IMF article was available only as substantive official publisher-indexed excerpts; claims are limited to those inspected passages.
